result.journal: Proc. ACM Meas. Anal. Comput. Syst.
result.keywords: We study a decentralized learning problem in which a population of agents repeatedly solves a shared stochastic multi-armed bandit task while exchanging sparse, asynchronous messages over a local communication graph. Each agent chooses an arm, decides whether to communicate, and updates its policy using only its own history together with limited peer observations. We propose a collaborative exploration protocol that shares compact arm summaries rather than raw rewards, enabling reduced regret under constrained bandwidth. The analysis characterizes per-agent regret as a function of the number of agents, the number of arms, the horizon, and the communication sparsity, and compares the method against both fully independent learning and fully connected information sharing. Empirical results on synthetic networked bandit instances show that minimal collaboration can substantially improve sample efficiency without incurring the cost of global synchronization.
result.title: Cooperative Exploration in Decentralized Bandit Networks.
